themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On proving downstream consent and deletion, all three models say enforcement stops at the boundary of systems you do not control, and the same opacity drives the answers on cross-channel incrementality, agentic traffic, and invisible B2B buying groups.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models put a proxy or gateway in front of every write, on downstream consent they gate every path data uses to leave the building, and on journey orchestration they route all sends through one shared eligibility check.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often changes while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization the models build a fixed panel of buyer questions because answers are stochastic and impression-less, on identity resolution they recruit consenting customers as a truth set, and on incrementality they install standing geo holdouts against platforms that adapt mid-test.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On governing generative content at volume all three models build a registry of pre-approved claims and restrict what tools may say, because deciding whether wording is properly supported stays a human reasoning task.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because whoever holds the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A schema or a standard cannot settle a fight over money and self-interest.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models say agents profit by posing as humans and offer perks or fast endpoints instead of rules, on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions a political settlement, and on journey orchestration they name channel owners paid on their own attributed revenue as the blocker.
